decisionLog.decision: BootFunc returns *server.Server (not a bare http.Handler) so the hub can wire per-project surfaces after boot — the header switcher via SetProjectSwitcher — while the slot stores srv.Handler(); the setup hot-swap callback checks the slot is still mounted before swapping and closes the boot if the project was removed mid-bootstrap.

Fragment templates render without pageData (a view struct is the dot), so the mount prefix reaches them through a per-renderer bp() template func registered at parse time; full-page templates use pageData.BasePath ($.BasePath inside ranges). app.js joins every URL with BASE read from body[data-base]. Legacy --dir mode keeps Base empty and renders byte-identical URLs.

Project switching lives in the breadcrumb trail, not a standalone header dropdown: hub mode renders the trail as Projects (root, → landing) → project name (→ that project's change list) → change/panel; single-project mode keeps the Changes root unchanged. The shipped Projects dropdown was removed (template, CSS, JS, and the BootFunc-*Server/SetProjectSwitcher wiring); pages expose data-base and data-project-name for the client-built trail instead.

The hub self-heals registry drift on read paths: rows()/ensureMounted mounts any registered project without a slot, retries slots stuck at unavailable (failed boots opened nothing), and unmounts slots whose registry entry vanished — the global registry file is the authority and the in-memory slot table converges to it. This also makes a second hub instance sharing the registry non-fatal: its additions mount here on the next landing look instead of sitting unmounted.

Legacy ledger parsing tolerates the backticked-ID convention (`id` where the canonical renderer emits bare ids) on - Change ID: and - Task: headers, so hand/GPT-authored legacy repos migrate on formatting alone; genuine data problems (prose dependency cells like None or ACC-00 through ACC-06) still refuse the migration and surface verbatim on the projects landing via a visible detail line.
